data.title: The last receipt

memoryNodes.cue: A tip can be added separately.
The tutor compares costs and income.
Providing drinking water has a cost.
memoryNodes.cueZh: 提供饮用水会产生成本。

data.situation:
After lunch, Lin carried her cup to the cafe counter. The bill had a line headed Gratuity, with nothing printed beside it. She asked what it meant. The cafe owner explained that it was a space for a tip if she wanted to leave one. Lin paid for the soup and added a small amount; no one told her that every visitor had to do the same. River Street Cafe
Soup: £3.00
Bread roll: £0.80
Gratuity: ______
Total food charge: £3.80
Any tip is optional and is added separately. In a quiet corner of the hall, a tutor was waiting beside a small budget sheet. Her short session taught financial skills such as recording costs and comparing them with income. Maya brought the market's receipts. Buying reusable cups had been an investment: the organisers had spent money now in the hope of saving on cups at later events. The tutor asked them to check the actual costs before assuming that it had worked. Tutor: You don't need a fortune to begin keeping clear records. Put a little aside each month and see what you accumulate over time.
Maya: The provision of drinking water also has a cost. We hired a dispenser for the courtyard.
Tutor: Put that on the sheet.
Lin: I wrote the wrong colour beside the cups.
Tutor: That's a trivial detail for this calculation. The number of cups and the amount paid matter more. When the last visitor left, Lin returned the map to the entrance desk. Maya folded the programme and put the receipts in an envelope. The market would return next year, but the figures on this year's sheet would help them decide what to keep. On the way home, Lin bought nothing else. The loaf was warm against her arm.

readingBlocks.en: After lunch, Lin carried her cup to the cafe counter. The bill had a line headed Gratuity, with nothing printed beside it. She asked what it meant. The cafe owner explained that it was a space for a tip if she wanted to leave one. Lin paid for the soup and added a small amount; no one told her that every visitor had to do the same.
readingBlocks.zh: 午餐后，林把杯子拿到咖啡馆柜台。账单有一行标着“小费”，旁边没有印金额。她问是什么意思。店主解释说，如果她想留小费，可以填在那里。林支付汤的钱，并添了一小笔；没人告诉她每位访客都必须这样做。

readingBlocks.en:
River Street Cafe
Soup: £3.00
Bread roll: £0.80
Gratuity: ______
Total food charge: £3.80
Any tip is optional and is added separately.
readingBlocks.zh:
河街咖啡馆
汤：三英镑
小面包：八十便士
小费：______
食物费用总计：三英镑八十便士
小费可自愿添加，另行计入。
readingBlocks.title: At the cafe counter

readingBlocks.en: In a quiet corner of the hall, a tutor was waiting beside a small budget sheet. Her short session taught financial skills such as recording costs and comparing them with income. Maya brought the market's receipts. Buying reusable cups had been an investment: the organisers had spent money now in the hope of saving on cups at later events. The tutor asked them to check the actual costs before assuming that it had worked.
readingBlocks.zh: 会堂一个安静角落里，老师坐在一张小预算表旁等着。她的短课教授记录成本、与收入比较等财务技能。玛雅带来了集市收据。买可重复使用的杯子是一项投入：组织者现在花钱，希望以后的活动能少花杯子钱。老师让她们先查实际成本，再判断是否如愿。

readingBlocks.en:
Tutor: You don't need a fortune to begin keeping clear records. Put a little aside each month and see what you accumulate over time.
Maya: The provision of drinking water also has a cost. We hired a dispenser for the courtyard.
Tutor: Put that on the sheet.
Lin: I wrote the wrong colour beside the cups.
Tutor: That's a trivial detail for this calculation. The number of cups and the amount paid matter more.
readingBlocks.zh:
老师：开始把账记清楚，不需要一大笔钱。每月留出一点，看看时间久了能积累多少。
玛雅：提供饮用水也有成本。我们为院子租了一台饮水设备。
老师：把那一项写进表里。
林：我在杯子旁边写错了颜色。
老师：对这次计算而言，那是无关紧要的细节。杯子数量和付款金额更重要。

readingBlocks.en: When the last visitor left, Lin returned the map to the entrance desk. Maya folded the programme and put the receipts in an envelope. The market would return next year, but the figures on this year's sheet would help them decide what to keep. On the way home, Lin bought nothing else. The loaf was warm against her arm.
readingBlocks.zh: 最后一位访客离开后，林把地图放回入口桌。玛雅折好节目单，把收据放进信封。明年集市还会再办，但今年表里的数字能帮助她们决定保留哪些安排。回家路上，林没有再买东西。那条面包贴着她的手臂，还是暖的。

glossary.note: 较正式的账单用语，常见词为tip；本店选择不推导为所有地区规则，退休补贴另义待确认。
glossary.example: Lin adds a small gratuity to the cafe bill.
glossary.exampleZh: 林在咖啡馆账单上添了一小笔小费。

externalEvidence.definition: a relatively small amount of money given for services rendered (as by a waiter)

glossary.note: 处理收支的技能，包括记录成本、预算与比较收入。
glossary.example: The session teaches financial skills such as recording costs.
glossary.exampleZh: 这堂短课教授记录成本等财务技能。

glossary.zh: 为将来收益或好处投入的钱或物
glossary.note: 可数名词，这里指值得购买、预期将来有用的东西；例如多次活动都能使用的杯子。
glossary.example: Buying reusable cups was an investment for future events.
glossary.exampleZh: 购买可重复使用的杯子，是为未来活动作的一项投入。

externalEvidence.findingZh: 可数名词也可指值得购买、将来有用的东西；本例可重复使用的杯子。

glossary.note: 可数名词a fortune；按原词义教学，与幸运义分开。
glossary.example: You do not need a fortune to begin keeping records.
glossary.exampleZh: 开始记账不需要一大笔钱。

externalEvidence.definition: a large amount of wealth or prosperity

glossary.note: 本句不及物，表示钱逐渐积累；原例主动积累财富也保留在来源记录。
glossary.example: Small amounts can accumulate over time.
glossary.exampleZh: 小额的钱可以随时间逐渐积累。

glossary.note: provision of + 服务或物资，表示提供行为；与make provision for准备安排区分。
glossary.example: The provision of drinking water has a cost.
glossary.exampleZh: 提供饮用水会产生成本。

externalEvidence.definition: the activity of supplying or providing something

glossary.note: 重要程度取决于当前任务；杯子颜色对这次成本计算不重要。
glossary.example: The cup colour is a trivial detail in this cost calculation.
glossary.exampleZh: 杯子颜色在这次成本计算中是无关紧要的细节。

retrievalPrompts.cue: A friend asks what the extra blank line on the bill means. Explain it.
retrievalPrompts.cueZh: 朋友问账单上额外的空白一行是什么意思。解释给对方。
acceptableAnswers: It is for a gratuity, or tip. At this cafe, it is optional and added separately.
checks: 按情境表达，允许其他自然说法

retrievalPrompts.cue: Explain what the short budgeting session teaches and why the organisers bought reusable cups.
retrievalPrompts.cueZh: 说明预算短课教什么，以及组织者为何买可重复使用的杯子。
acceptableAnswers: It teaches financial skills such as recording costs. The cups were an investment for future events.
checks: 按情境表达，允许其他自然说法

retrievalPrompts.cue: Explain why the water dispenser belongs on the cost sheet and why the cup colour is less important.
retrievalPrompts.cueZh: 说明饮水设备为何应记入成本表，以及杯子颜色为何较不重要。
acceptableAnswers: The provision of drinking water costs money. The cup colour is a trivial detail in this calculation.
checks: 按情境表达，允许其他自然说法

transferPrompt.cue: A student thinks saving is pointless without a large amount of money. Offer a simple alternative without promising a return.
transferPrompt.cueZh: 学生觉得没有大笔钱就不值得储蓄。提供一个简单替代思路，不承诺回报。
acceptableAnswers: You do not need a fortune. Small amounts can accumulate over time.
checks: 按情境表达，允许其他自然说法
